key_insight: Naive Bayes and linear SVM accurately distinguished scam from legitimate Ghanaian mobile-money SMS in a small, structured corpus.
engineering_relevance: Classical text classifiers offer a promising lightweight approach to carrier- or handset-level fraud filtering in low-resource settings.
method: Normalise currency amounts, phone numbers, and USSD codes.
Encode SMS text using TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams.
Compare Multinomial Naive Bayes, linear SVM, and Random Forest.
evidence_signal: On 220 labelled messages across 18 subcategories, five-fold cross-validation accuracy averaged 96.6% for Naive Bayes, 94.9% for SVM, and 92.0% for Random Forest; Naive Bayes and SVM achieved 1.00 accuracy, F1, and AUC on the 20% held-out test set.
watch_item: Perfect held-out scores on a small, template-based corpus may not generalise to naturalistic, multilingual messages or evolving scams.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers
